2026-11-24: Fixture examples/pretty-midi-roundtrip covers note-level build, read-back, tempo-change times, pitch bends and piano roll. pretty_midi 0.2.11.post0 has no public tempo-authoring call; the fixture sets the tempo map through private _tick_scales.

evidence.result: Two instruments, five notes, tempo 120 to 60 BPM at 1.0 s, two piano pitch bends; read back with 0.0 s note and bend error (tolerance one 60 BPM tick, 0.00208 s); tempo times [0.0, 1.0]; end 2.5 s; fs=8 piano roll 128x20 with 28 cells exact; two separate-process writes byte-identical, 147 bytes, SHA-256 65d76b26f7ed080fac80e217a92c1acf8e834cc2ac397e3c682fd26cb1fc967e. mido 1.3.3, numpy 2.5.5, Python 3.12.13, macOS 26.6 arm64.
evidence.scope: Note-level MIDI build, tempo change, pitch bends, read-back, piano roll fs=8, identical reruns; tempo set via private API; no synthesis; macOS arm64

summary: Python MIDI utilities for inspecting, modifying and writing musical note data. It offers a note-oriented representation; optional synthesis and external instruments require separate dependencies.
use_when: Manipulate symbolic MIDI notes in Python
Explore editable music variants rather than audio-only changes
avoid_when: Process audio recordings: FFmpeg or librosa
Need low-level MIDI message operations: Mido
license: MIT (library code, read from the installed LICENSE.txt on 2026-11-24); bundled TimGM6mb.sf2 soundfont and dependency terms need review

install.macos: Create a Python 3.12 virtual environment and run `pip install pretty_midi==0.2.11.post0`; pinned set in examples/pretty-midi-roundtrip/requirements.txt

assessment.rationale: Official sources describe an automation route; release and substantive-commit dates could not be fully established. Keep candidate pending further review.
